To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
before establishment of true cell polarization, the plasma membrane is already polarized on an ultrastuctural level.

syntaxins are concentrated in mutually exclusive, sub-micron-sized clusters in non-polarized epithelial cells, and that the formation of syntaxin clusters depends on different mechanisms for syntaxin 3 (microtubule-dependent) and syntaxin 4 (actin filament-dependent).
syntaxins 3, and 4 are sorted into mutually exclusive submicron clusters in the absence of polarity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of syntaxins in the establishment of cell and tissue polarity.
the mechanisms of membrane trafficking and the establishment of cellular polarity in epithelial cells.
how cells establish polarity and how they use polarity to regulate cell growth and cell movement.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the syntaxin 3/4 clusters are not a result of cell polarity establishment but are a result of the sorting of syntaxins 3/4 to the apical or basolateral membrane domains, respectively.

syntaxins 3 & 4 are localized to separate, mutually exclusive clusters in non-polarized epithelial cells, which is independent of the expression levels and the presence of the apical sorting signal of syntaxin3.
the syntaxin 3/4 clusters represent the first step in the sorting of SNAREs into their respective membrane domains.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the plasma membrane of polarized epithelial cells has a polarized organization at the ultrastructural level.
syntaxins 3/4 form distinct clusters on the cell surface before establishment of cell polarization.
syntaxins 3/4 are sorted into distinct clusters in a polarized manner before establishment of cell and tissue polarity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
SNARE proteins can form clusters on the cell surface that are not dependent on the presence of vesicles.
syntaxin 3 forms clusters in nonpolarized cells and that these clusters are required for apical targeting.
syntaxin clusters represent a new, fundamental feature of polarized membrane trafficking.
